newsitem.title: INDIA: India gold seen rising on political instability.
newsitem.headline: India gold seen rising on political instability.

text.p: Political uncertainty and wedding season demand helped gold prices rise in India over the past week, while a downtrend continued in Pakistan, dealers and analysts said on Monday.
They said political developments leading to the fall of India's 10-month-old minority coalition government on Friday left investors looking for fresh avenues.
"Gold is an obvious choice for investment at times of political crises, but demand for the metal has not picked up as expected," analyst Madhusudan Daga said.
In the week to Monday, standard gold prices rose 25 rupees, reaching 4,805 rupees per 10 grams.
Daga said part of the money leaving equities could find its way into bullion, adding, "Investors are waiting and watching the political situation."
Dealers said India's second marriage season, beginning in April and lasting up to end-May, could further fuel demand for gold.
They said a two-day strike by air traffic controllers at India's major airports last week had disrupted arrivals of imported gold.
They said the landed cost of imported gold was higher than the domestic price because of a surge in the premium paid to acquire special licences by dealers to buy gold from abroad.
Babubhai Jain, a leading bullion dealer, said gold supply had also been tight because of the limited sale of confiscated gold by customs.
The price of an imported gold biscuit (116.50 grams) was at 56,500 rupees against a domestic price of 56,200, dealers said.
Weak world prices might prompt fresh arrivals to the local market in the coming days, said Mahavir Shah, a Bombay jeweller.
In Pakistan's main commercial city of Karachi, gold prices were expected to remain mixed in the current week due to sluggish demand, dealers said.
"Low demand for gold from jewellers would keep prices depressed," said a dealer.
In the week to Monday, gold prices fell 48 rupees per 10 grams to 4,646 on the Karachi market.
In Dubai, dealers said they expected India's political turmoil to fuel gold demand in the Indian sub-continent and lift prices as anxious Indians turned to gold as a safe investment.
Dubai is the main feeder market for gold to the Indian sub-continent.
A shopping festival in Dubai, which opened on March 27, continued to drive gold sales upwards.
